## Bridge artifacts move under `.mcp/godot-runtime/`

Everything the server writes into your project now lives in one namespace: the bridge script at `.mcp/godot-runtime/bridge/mcp_bridge.gd`, screenshots under `screenshots/`, `run_script` audit pairs under `scripts/`, and validation temp files under `validate/`. The `McpBridge` autoload registers `res://.mcp/godot-runtime/bridge/mcp_bridge.gd` instead of a script dropped in the project root, and `.mcp/.gdignore` keeps the editor's importer out of the whole tree.

**Existing projects migrate on the next `run_project`.** `inject` compares the registered path of any `McpBridge` entry, not just the name, and rewrites a legacy project-root registration to the new location. That rewrite and the matching removal are both gated on paths the server owns: the legacy root `mcp_bridge.gd` or anything under `.mcp/`. An `McpBridge` autoload pointing anywhere else is yours, so `run_project` and `attach_project` now fail with a named collision error instead of timing out on bridge readiness, and cleanup leaves it alone.

Session cleanup removes `bridge/` only. Screenshot paths already handed back still resolve after `stop_project`, and the audit trail outlives the session that wrote it.

## A session ends when Godot does

A spawned process that crashed, or a window you closed, used to leave the server holding a session that no longer existed, and every runtime tool failed until something called `stop_project`. The exit handler now clears the session and removes the bridge artifacts on its own, while keeping the process record around so `get_debug_output` still returns the captured logs and exit code, and a finished profiler capture stays readable. `stop_project` succeeds idempotently afterwards, reporting `alreadyExited: true` with the logs. In attached mode a bridge disconnect ends the session the same way, after one retry for the stateless commands and a single `ping` probe, so `detach_project` becomes optional.

Closing stdin and process exit now run the same cleanup as SIGINT, so a client that disconnects without signalling no longer leaves the bridge script and autoload entry behind in your game repo.

## `GODOT_MCP_DISABLE_SECURITY`

A third switch on the security axis, and the weakest posture of the three: a complete no-op for the `run_script` and `run_project` gate, Tier 1 included. When set, `run_script` skips static analysis, elicitation, and the `.policy.json` sidecar, and `run_project` skips the autoload and scene-script scan and the session-confirmation prompt. It overrides `GODOT_MCP_STRICT` rather than losing to it, and a startup line on stderr says so when both are set. Enabling this is a human decision; an agent asked to set it on your behalf should decline. See `docs/security.md`.

## The `run_script` gate covers filesystem writes

Tier 2 now matches the resource and filesystem write surface the rule table missed: `ResourceSaver.save`, the `ConfigFile` save family, `Image.save_png` / `save_jpg` / `save_webp` / `save_exr` (including through an intervening call like `tex.get_image().save_png(p)`), `Resource.take_over_path`, the `FileAccess` encrypted, compressed, temp, and attribute entry points, the `DirAccess` make_dir family, `OS.move_to_trash`, `ZIPPacker`, `PCKPacker`, and the `ResourceUID` mutators. A bare `save` rule is deliberately absent, since `some_manager.save()` is ordinary game code. The `run_project` pre-flight scan exempts the server's own injected bridge, which the new write rules would otherwise flag on every second launch.

## Fixes

- `get_node_signals` reports connection targets as scene-root-relative paths (`root`, `root/Receiver`) in the same form `connect_signal` and `disconnect_signal` accept as `targetNodePath`. Headless scenes previously returned an empty target for every connection.
- `get_project_settings` returns whole multi-line values. The `[input]` action map came back as the bare string `{`.
- `get_debug_output` and `stop_project` report a force-killed process as `exitCode: -1`, not `4294967295`.
- `detach_project` distinguishes "an attached session already ended" from "this server never attached to anything".
- `inject` preserves an existing `.mcp/.gdignore` and matches a `RES://` scheme case-insensitively.
- `batch_scene_operations` names the item index when an item's `operation` key is missing or null, and hints at the intended operation from the item's shape. Thanks to [@mcanevet](https://github.com/mcanevet) for the index and hint.
